memberdef.name: popen_write_timeout

briefdescription.para: Write data to the child stdin.

detaileddescription.para: Yield until all count bytes will be written.
Returns count at success, otherwise returns -1 and set a diag.
Possible errors:

listitem.para:
IllegalParams: a parameter check fails:
count: data is too big.
flags: stdin is not set.
handle: handle does not support the requested IO operation.
handle: attempt to operate on a closed fd.
SocketError: an IO error occurs at write().
TimedOut: timeout quota is exceeded.
FiberIsCancelled: cancelled by an outside code.

detaileddescription.para: An error may occur after a partial write. There is not way to enquire amount of written bytes in the case.
FIXME: Provide an info re amount written bytes in the case. Say, return -(written) in the case.

memberdef.name: popen_read_timeout

briefdescription.para: Read data from a child's peer with timeout.

detaileddescription.para: Yield until some data will be available for read.
Returns amount of read bytes at success, otherwise returns -1 and set a diag.
Zero return value means EOF.
Note: Less then count bytes may be available for read at a moment, so a return value less then count does not mean EOF.
Possible errors:

listitem.para:
IllegalParams: a parameter check fails:
count: buffer is too big.
flags: stdout and stdrr are both set or both missed.
handle: handle does not support the requested IO operation.
handle: attempt to operate on a closed fd.
SocketError: an IO error occurs at read().
TimedOut: timeout quota is exceeded.
FiberIsCancelled: cancelled by an outside code.

briefdescription.para: Close parent's ends of std* fds.

detaileddescription.para: The following flags controls which fds should be closed:
POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDIN close parent's end of child's stdin POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDOUT close parent's end of child's stdout POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDERR close parent's end of child's stderr
The main reason to use this function is to send EOF to child's stdin. However parent's end of stdout / stderr may be closed too.

The function does not fail on already closed fds (idempotence). However it fails on attempt to close the end of a pipe that was never exist. In other words, a subset of ..._FD_STD{IN,OUT,ERR} flags used at a handle creation may be used here.
The function does not close any fds on a failure: either all requested fds are closed or neither of them.
Returns 0 at success, otherwise -1 and set a diag.
Possible errors:

listitem.para:
IllegalParams: a parameter check fails:
flags: neither stdin, stdout nor stderr is set.
handle: handle does not support the requested IO operation (one of fds is not piped).

briefdescription.para: Send a signal to a child process.

detaileddescription.para: When POPEN_FLAG_GROUP_SIGNAL is set the function sends a signal to a process group rather than a process.

A signal will not be sent if the child process is already dead: otherwise we might kill another process that occupies the same PID later. This means that if the child process dies before its own childs, the function will not send a signal to the process group even when ..._SETSID and ..._GROUP_SIGNAL are set.
Mac OS may don't deliver a signal to a processes in a group when ..._SETSID and ..._GROUP_SIGNAL are set. It seems there is a race here: when a process is just forked it may be not signaled.
Return 0 at success or -1 at failure (and set a diag).
Possible errors:

listitem.para: SystemError: a process does not exists anymore Aside of a non-exist process it is also set for a zombie process or when all processes in a group are zombies (but see note re Mac OS below).
SystemError: invalid signal number
SystemError: no permission to send a signal to a process or a process group
It is set on Mac OS when a signal is sent to a process group, where a group leader is zombie (or when all processes in it are zombies, don't sure).
Whether it may appear due to other reasons is unclear.

detaileddescription.para: Set errno to ESRCH when a process does not exist or is zombie.
Send SIGKILL and free the handle.
Details about signaling:

listitem.para: The signal is sent only when ...KEEP_CHILD is not set.
The signal is sent only when a process is alive according to the information available on current even loop iteration. (There is a gap here: a zombie may be signaled; it is harmless.)

The signal is sent to a process or a grocess group depending of ..._GROUP_SIGNAL flag.
popen_send_signal() for note about ..._GROUP_SIGNAL. Resources are released disregarding of whether a signal sending succeeds: all fds occupied by the handle are closed, the handle is removed from a living list, all occupied memory is freed.

detaileddescription.para: The function may return 0 or -1 (and set a diag) as usual, but it always frees the handle resources. So any return value usually means success for a caller. The return value and diagnostics are purely informational: it is for logging or same kind of reporting.
Possible diagnostics (don't consider them as errors):

listitem.para: SystemError: no permission to send a signal to a process or a process group

This error may appear due to Mac OS behaviour on zombies when ..._GROUP_SIGNAL is set,
popen_send_signal(). Whether it may appear due to other reasons is unclear.

detaileddescription.para: Always return 0 when a process is known as dead: no signal will be send, so no 'failure' may appear.

This function creates a new child process and passes it pipe ends to communicate with child's stdin/stdout/stderr depending on opts:flags. Where opts:flags could be the bitwise "OR" for the following values:
POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDIN - to write to stdin POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDOUT - to read from stdout POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDERR - to read from stderr
When need to pass /dev/null descriptor into a child the following values can be used:
POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDIN_DEVNULL POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDOUT_DEVNULL POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDERR_DEVNULL
These flags have no effect if appropriate POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDx flags are set.
When need to completely close the descriptors the following values can be used:
POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDIN_CLOSE POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDOUT_CLOSE POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDERR_CLOSE
These flags have no effect if appropriate POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDx flags are set.
If none of POPEN_FLAG_FD_STDx flags are specified the child process will run with all files inherited from a parent.
Returns pointer to a new popen handle on success, otherwise NULL returned and an error is set to the diagnostics area.
Possible errors:

listitem.para:
IllegalParams: a parameter check fails:
group signal is set, while setsid is not.
SystemError: dup(), fcntl(), pipe(), vfork() or close() fails in the parent process.
SystemError: (temporary restriction) one of std{in,out,err} is closed in the parent process.
OutOfMemory: unable to allocate handle.

detaileddescription.para: Kills all running children and frees resources.
